arguments: {"summary": "Snapshot is the Netty 5.0.0.Final-SNAPSHOT tree (2019-era codebase, 1832 visible files). After reviewing the HTTP codec, HTTP/2 codec, compression codecs, codec-haproxy, SSL handler paths, resolver/common and transport code, plus grep sweeps (exec, Java deserialization, XML factories, Random, temp files, bounds helpers), the strongest concrete issue is a parser differential in HttpObjectDecoder: whitespace between a header name and its colon is stripped and the canonicalized header is then used for message framing, so inputs like Transfer-Encoding : chunked or Content-Length : N are silently normalized. Default header validation cannot catch this because validation sees the already-trimmed name. This is a request-smuggling pattern (CWE-444) with clear remote input control. One candidate is submitted; other plausible leads are listed as rejected.", "candidates": [{"id": "netty-http-header-whitespace-smuggling", "title": "HTTP request smuggling via whitespace between header name and colon in HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader", "weakness_type": "CWE-444 HTTP Request Smuggling (parser differential / improper input validation)", "root_cause": "HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader() terminates the header field-name at the first whitespace character (Character.isWhitespace) and then scans forward to the colon, so a line such as 'Transfer-Encoding : chunked' is parsed as name=Transfer-Encoding, value=chunked. The whitespace is discarded before the name reaches DefaultHttpHeaders.HttpNameValidator, which would otherwise reject a space inside a header name. The decoder therefore silently accepts and canonicalizes a header line that other HTTP components reject or parse differently, and the canonicalized name is used unchanged for body-framing decisions (Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length).", "locations": [{"path": "codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpObjectDecoder.java", "start_line": 716, "end_line": 747}, {"path": "codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpObjectDecoder.java", "start_line": 564, "end_line": 616}, {"path": "codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpObjectDecoder.java", "start_line": 625, "end_line": 674}, {"path": "codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpUtil.java", "start_line": 303, "end_line": 305}, {"path": "codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/DefaultHttpHeaders.java", "start_line": 374, "end_line": 397}], "attacker_control": "A remote peer fully controls the raw HTTP byte stream (request or response) and can insert whitespace (space or tab) between any header field-name and the colon, for example Transfer-Encoding : chunked or Content-Length : N.", "prerequisites": "A Netty HTTP decoder (HttpRequestDecoder / HttpServerCodec, or HttpResponseDecoder / HttpClientCodec) is used in a deployment where another HTTP-aware component (reverse proxy, load balancer, cache, WAF or upstream server) parses the same message. The attacker must be able to send a message whose meaning differs between that component and Netty. validateHeaders=true (the default) does not prevent the issue.", "trace": "1) HttpObjectDecoder.decode() enters READ_HEADER (lines 213-218). 2) readHeaders() reads a line via headerParser (line 568) and calls splitHeader() (line 585). 3) In splitHeader (716-747) the name loop breaks on colon or any whitespace (725-730); the colon loop then skips ahead to the colon (732-737); name is the substring before the whitespace (739) and value the substring after the colon (740-746). 4) Back in readHeaders the canonicalized pair is stored via headers.add(name, value) (583, 597). 5) Framing is decided from the canonicalized headers: HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked (HttpUtil.java 303-305) returns true for the accepted Transfer-Encoding: chunked pair and selects READ_CHUNK_SIZE (HttpObjectDecoder 608-609); otherwise contentLength() (618-623) uses the trimmed Content-Length value for READ_FIXED_LENGTH_CONTENT (610-611). The same splitHeader is used for trailers (line 654).", "impact": "HTTP request/response desynchronization (smuggling) between Netty and another parsing component: an intermediary can ignore or reject the whitespace-padded header while Netty honors it as Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length (or the reverse when Netty acts as client). This enables request queuing/poisoning effects such as bypassing upstream access controls, cache poisoning, or routing a hidden request, depending on the surrounding stack.", "counterevidence_checked": "Default HTTP name validation (DefaultHttpHeaders.validateHeaderNameElement, 350-397) rejects spaces, tabs and separators inside names, but splitHeader removes the whitespace before the name is validated, so validation cannot catch this input; validateHeaders=false only widens acceptance. Header value validation (DefaultHttpHeaders.HeaderValueConverterAndValidator, 426-490) blocks CRLF inside values and is not relevant here. No maximum header size bypass is needed; the crafted line fits within maxHeaderSize. I found no in-repo test asserting rejection of whitespace before a colon. The public decoders reach this path. Exploitation still requires a second HTTP component with divergent parsing, so this is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed exploit.", "confidence": "medium", "unverified": "Not runtime tested; no build, tests or scanners were run. No git history, upstream fix or CVE database is available in this run, so the exact upstream fix revision/mapping is not verified; only the source behavior described above is verified by reading. Practical exploitation depends on deployment topology (an intermediary with different parsing)."}], "rejected_leads": [{"lead": "Duplicate or conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding handling: HttpUtil.getContentLength (codec-http/.../HttpUtil.java:174-189) returns the first Content-Length value and HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders (564-616) does not reject duplicate Content-Length headers or Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length.", "reason": "Related but distinct request-smuggling root cause with weaker direct source evidence, and the desync again depends on a divergent peer. The whitespace/parser-normalization bug was selected as the single strongest candidate instead of splitting the smuggling area."}, {"lead": "Unbounded decompression output allocation in JdkZlibDecoder (codec/.../compression/JdkZlibDecoder.java:180-212) growing a heap buffer from inflated input.", "reason": "Growth is derived from inflater input remaining rather than an attacker-declared size, and no concrete unbounded-allocation condition could be traced; evidence threshold not met."}, {"lead": "HTTP/2 header / content-length validation gaps (HpackDecoder, DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder) potentially enabling h2-to-h1 desync.", "reason": "No concrete attacker-controlled path with divergent interpretation was traced in this snapshot; left unconfirmed."}, {"lead": "Java deserialization in the serialization codecs (ObjectDecoder / ObjectDecoderInputStream using CompactObjectInputStream with a ClassResolver).", "reason": "This is the documented purpose of those codecs and is guarded by a configurable ClassResolver; no snapshot-specific defect was identified."}, {"lead": "XmlDecoder (codec-xml) does not explicitly disable external entity resolution on the Aalto factory.", "reason": "Aalto default behavior cannot be verified from this source alone and no concrete XXE flow was demonstrated; insufficient evidence."}], "coverage_summary": "Reviewed the assigned tree (1832 visible files).
